purpose: Add Low-Quality Image Placeholder (LQIP) and Dominant Color placeholder support for lazy-loaded images, replacing a hardcoded gray SVG with three user-selectable placeholder types (None, SVG with dominant color, Dominant Color, LQIP).
riskRationale: Critical data-loss bug: commit_img_info() does not merge dominant_color/lqip arrays, causing concurrent conversion jobs to silently overwrite each other's placeholder data. Important issues: dominant-color background-color transition is invisible behind the colored SVG src, IntersectionObserver fallback path (older browsers) has no placeholder effects, and placeholder extraction is skipped for WebP/GIF source images.
breakingChanges: The private method post_process_svg_placeholders() was renamed to post_process_placeholders() with a changed signature
The replacePlaceholderWithSVG boolean setting was replaced with placeholderType string (migration included)

text: Well-architected implementation following existing codebase patterns (deferred commit, atomic updates, WP_HTML_Tag_Processor) with clean backward compatibility, efficient dominant color extraction, and smooth LQIP blur/unblur CSS transitions. However, a critical concurrent data-loss bug in commit_img_info() must be fixed, and several important issues around placeholder visibility, older-browser fallback, and WebP/GIF extraction gaps need addressing.

reasoning: The commit_img_info() race condition will silently corrupt placeholder data under concurrent image conversion jobs. This is the blocking issue. Additional important issues (dominant color SVG invisibility, fallback path gaps, WebP/GIF extraction) must also be resolved before merge.

message: Clean backward-compatibility migration from replacePlaceholderWithSVG to placeholderType with proper ternary fallback and default-setting alignment.
get_placeholder_src_for_image() gracefully degrades to gray SVG when placeholder data is missing, and per-request path caching avoids redundant DB/filesystem I/O.
Dominant color extraction uses reduced-stride pixel sampling with proper fallback for empty images, balancing accuracy against performance.
Placeholder data stored via the existing deferred-commit pattern (update_img_info_atomic), maintaining consistency with the rest of the image info system.

IntersectionObserver handler applies dominant-color background and LQIP blur classes BEFORE setting the real image src, preventing white flash. Load event handler properly cleans up with self-removing listeners.
The wppo-lqip-loaded transition transitions blur OFF only (not ON), preventing jarring blur-in when the placeholder first appears.
sanitize_image_info_for_client() correctly drops dominant_color and lqip arrays from client-exposed data, preventing filesystem paths from leaking to the browser.
Correctly scoped the JumbledIncrementer exclusion to only the specific file with the false positive, rather than globally disabling the rule.

commit_img_info() merges 'pending', 'completed', and 'failed' arrays from live and deferred state, but does NOT merge 'dominant_color' and 'lqip' arrays. Under concurrent conversion jobs (e.g., Action Scheduler + upload), the last shutdown hook to run will silently overwrite placeholder data for all images processed by the other concurrent request, causing permanent data loss of placeholder data.
suggestion: Add merge logic for dominant_color and lqip arrays in commit_img_info(), mirroring the existing pattern for status arrays. Use array_merge() to combine live and deferred entries keyed by relative path.

message: dominant_color placeholder generates a colored SVG as the img src (via generate_svg_base64) and also sets data-wppo-dominant-color as background-color. The colored SVG completely fills the img element, making the CSS background-color invisible behind it. When the real image loads, users see the SVG abruptly replaced by the real image — the smooth color fade transition is hidden behind the opaque SVG.
suggestion: For dominant_color type, use a transparent 1x1 pixel SVG or transparent data URI as src instead of a colored SVG. The background-color alone will show through on the transparent placeholder, making the fade transition visible to the user.

message: The lazyLoadFallback function (scroll-based fallback for browsers without IntersectionObserver) does not apply data-wppo-dominant-color background-color or data-wppo-lqip class before setting the image src, and does not attach load event listeners for cleanup. Users on older browsers will see no placeholder effect at all.
suggestion: Add the same dominant-color background and LQIP class logic to the lazyLoadFallback image-processing branch (the else block at line 558), and attach the same self-removing load event listener for cleanup, mirroring the IntersectionObserver path at lines 349-411.

message: The WebP (line 312) and GIF (line 365) early-return branches both exit before the placeholder extraction code at lines 412-418 runs. Uploaded WebP or GIF source images will never have dominant_color or LQIP data stored, even if they are successfully converted to other formats.
suggestion: Move placeholder extraction into a shared helper function called from each successful conversion path before early returns. For WebP sources, extract from the GD resource before imagedestroy. For GIF sources, create a GD resource from the Imagick result and extract.

message: No cleanup mechanism for dominant_color or lqip entries when images are deleted from the media library. Over time, these arrays will accumulate orphaned entries for deleted images, causing unbounded growth of the wppo_img_info option.
suggestion: Hook into delete_attachment to remove the corresponding placeholder entries from wppo_img_info when an image is deleted.

message: get_placeholder_src_for_image() calls Img_Converter::get_img_info() which loads the entire wppo_img_info option (potentially hundreds of KB for large media libraries) into memory on every page view when dominant_color or lqip placeholder types are active. While the result is statically cached per-request, the initial load cost is paid regardless. On sites with thousands of converted images, this adds significant memory overhead to every front-end request.
suggestion: Store dominant_color and lqip lookups in a separate, slimmer option or implement a targeted custom table query instead of loading the entire image info blob. At minimum, document the memory impact for large media libraries.

message: generate_lqip() does not account for transparent PNG/GIF images. The imagecopyresampled() copies RGBA pixels into a truecolor resource, but imagejpeg() does not support alpha — transparent areas render as black in the JPEG LQIP, causing a visible dark flash before the real image loads.
suggestion: Fill the thumbnail with white (or the dominant color) using imagefill() before resampling, or generate a PNG LQIP using imagepng() at quality 6 for transparency support.

message: Error suppression operator @imagejpeg() hides legitimate failures. If GD encounters an allocation error or memory limit, the warning is suppressed and $success becomes false, but the root cause is invisible.
suggestion: Remove @ suppression and log failures when WP_DEBUG is enabled.

message: The post_process_placeholders() regex pattern #<img\b[^>]*data-src=[\"']...[\"'][^>]*>#i can match data-src inside other attributes (e.g., inline event handlers) if an attacker crafts a malicious tag with data-src preceded by other quoted strings.
suggestion: Use \sdata-src instead of just data-src to require an attribute-boundary whitespace before the attribute.

message: After an image loads, data-wppo-dominant-color and data-wppo-lqip attributes remain on the DOM element even though they are no longer needed. The background-color is set to 'transparent' and blur classes are removed, but the data attributes persist, adding minor bloat to the live DOM.
suggestion: Remove data-wppo-dominant-color and data-wppo-lqip attributes in the load event handler after handling their effects, using el.removeAttribute().

message: Placeholder descriptions conditionally render based on the current selected value, only showing the description for the currently-selected type. A user must select each option to understand what it does, rather than seeing all descriptions at once or having a persistent help tooltip.
suggestion: Consider showing all option descriptions in a persistent help area, or add a tooltip accessible via hover/focus on each <option> element.

message: The sample_rate formula max(1, (int)(min($width, $height) / 20)) uses a fixed 20-step sample. For very wide panoramas (e.g., 10000x500), the sample_rate is 25, sampling only ~80 pixels total, which may produce an inaccurate dominant color.
suggestion: Use a minimum pixel count floor (e.g., at least 500 samples) instead of a fixed divisor of 20, to ensure accuracy for both small and large non-square images.

message: LQIP thumbnail height has no upper bound. For very tall images (e.g., 200x3000), the 20px-wide scaled thumb would be 300px tall, producing a large base64 data URI.
suggestion: Cap thumb_height to a reasonable maximum (e.g., 200px) to prevent excessively large placeholder data URIs.

message: get_placeholder_type() returns the raw option value without validating it is one of the four allowed values (none/svg/dominant_color/lqip). An unrecognized value causes get_placeholder_src_for_image() to fall through and return an empty result with no placeholder.
suggestion: Add validation to return 'none' for unrecognized values.
